statement: Whenever last_stone_weight(stones) returns a result r, r is the terminal value of the following game. Start with the multiset S = {stones[0], ..., stones[len(stones)-1]}. While S has at least two elements, let y be a maximum element of S and let x be a maximum element of S after deleting one occurrence of y (so x <= y are the two largest elements, with ties allowed); delete one occurrence of x and one occurrence of y, and if y > x insert one occurrence of y - x, while if y = x insert nothing. When S has at most one element, r is the sole element if S is nonempty and r = 0 if S is empty. This terminal value is independent of which equal largest elements are chosen at a tie.
preconditions: stones is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, last_stone_weight(stones) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, access out of bounds, or perform an out-of-range 64-bit arithmetic operation. Every stone weight occurring during the game is a nonnegative integer at most 1000, so all subtractions y - x stay within the 64-bit range.
preconditions: stones is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, 0 <= r <= max{stones[i] | 0 <= i < len(stones)}.
preconditions: stones is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r is congruent to the total sum sum_{i=0}^{len(stones)-1} stones[i] modulo 2.
preconditions: stones is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = stones[0].
preconditions: stones is a valid input (1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000 for every i) and len(stones) = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = |stones[0] - stones[1]|.
preconditions: stones is a valid input (1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000 for every i) and len(stones) = 2.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = w if n is odd, and r = 0 if n is even.
preconditions: stones is a valid input with n = len(stones) >= 3, and there is a weight w with 1 <= w <= 1000 such that stones[i] = w for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the two calls return results, last_stone_weight(stones) = last_stone_weight(stones').
preconditions: stones and stones' are two valid inputs (each length between 1 and 30, each entry between 1 and 1000), and stones' is a permutation of stones, i.e. the two slices have the same length and the same multiset of weights.

statement: Whenever both calls return results, last_stone_weight(scaled) = c * last_stone_weight(stones).
preconditions: stones is a valid input, c is a positive integer, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= c * stones[i] <= 1000; let scaled be the valid slice with scaled[i] = c * stones[i].

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = stones[m] - sum_{0 <= i < len(stones), i != m} stones[i].
preconditions: stones is a valid input and there exists an index m with 0 <= m < len(stones) such that stones[m] > sum_{0 <= i < len(stones), i != m} stones[i].

statement: Whenever both calls return results, last_stone_weight(stones) = last_stone_weight(stones').
preconditions: stones is a valid input with n = len(stones) >= 3, M = max{stones[i] | 0 <= i < n}, and at least two indices p < q with stones[p] = stones[q] = M; let stones' be the slice of length n - 2 obtained by deleting stones[p] and stones[q].

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r < max{stones[i] | 0 <= i < len(stones)}.
preconditions: stones is a valid input with len(stones) >= 2, and not all entries of stones are equal, i.e. there exist i and j with stones[i] != stones[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = 0.
preconditions: stones is a valid input and there exists an index m with 0 <= m < len(stones) such that stones[m] = sum_{0 <= i < len(stones), i != m} stones[i].

statement: Whenever the function returns r, there exist signs e_i in {-1, +1} for i = 0, ..., len(stones)-1 such that r = |sum_{i=0}^{len(stones)-1} e_i * stones[i]|.
preconditions: stones is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(stones) <= 30 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000.
